parsed.explanation: No trans-specific exposure is documented: no criminalisation of gender expression, no border/document/facility rules reaching trans visitors, no trans incidents recorded, and the two assaults are from 2005–2006 (dated, isolated, one against visitors who were unharmed elsewhere on tour). Sexual-orientation incidents weigh only secondarily. Negatives: the 2007 anti-discrimination provision omits gender identity, recourse for anti-trans treatment is unproven, and a political party has a documented hostility record (through 2015) — a societal-hostility-with-thin-recourse signal, tier 3 at most. Dated hostility plus organized public pushback and legal same-sex conduct since 1933 place this moderately below acceptance-with-protections jurisdictions but well above any criminalising regime. Uncertainty is genuine: thin data cannot confirm current police or public handling of a trans visitor.

entry_documents.exposure: No document or marker rules affecting trans visitors are documented.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented border interaction reaching visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No trans detention or custody cases documented; 2006 police refusal to handle an assault predates the 2007 provision.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No later sourced account of police handling of anti-LGBT complaints.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility, bathroom or ward rules affecting trans visitors documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Parent-state facility rules not documented as applying.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Political hostility documented: party formally opposed to homosexuality, leader demanded Pride ban and route changes (2010–2015); anti-discrimination law omits gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Organised public pushback documented (singer urging defiance; petitions).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostility is toward public expression, dated to 2015; no state targeting of trans people shown.

minors_guardians.exposure: Nothing specific to travelling minors or guardians documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two dated attacks: 2006 severe assault on a gay public figure (police refused the case pre-2007) and 2005 chase of a visiting drag group in the capital only. No trans-specific incident documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Visiting drag group unattacked elsewhere on tour; no post-2007 incidents recorded.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: 2007 provision could in principle offer recourse, but no prosecutions sourced.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender identity excluded from the anti-discrimination ground list; current police practice and partnership status unresolved in the record.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal same-sex conduct since 1933; functioning institutions assumed only partially evidenced.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin-data jurisdiction: unknowns resolve toward structural facts, not neutrality.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra imposes a universal, state-run visitor exclusion register. This dossier documents no traveller-facing state mechanism at all — no register, no entry bar, no targeting — so it sits clearly above 0.35.

Kestrel Isles show routine discretionary secondary screening of divergent documents. Here no border or screening exposure is documented; only dated societal hostility and a coverage gap in anti-discrimination law, so this rates slightly above 0.55.

Meridia offers trained border officers, a working tribunal, and release-after-detention remedies. This dossier lacks any documented working trans-inclusive remedy (gender identity omitted from the provision), so it sits a step below 0.75.
Saruth detains trans visitors in abusive cells with state complicity. Nothing comparable exists here: no trans arrests, no custody evidence, no organised targeting — far above 0.15.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a small, thinly documented self-governing jurisdiction with no trans-specific traveller exposure on record: no gender-expression criminalisation, no border, facility, custody or care rules reaching trans visitors, and no trans-specific incident ever documented. The documented negatives are societal and political — a party hostile to LGBT public expression (dated 2010–2015), two old LGB-flagged assaults from 2005–2006 with one pre-2007 police refusal — which are secondary for a trans visitor and constitute tier-3 societal hostility at most. The 2007 anti-discrimination provision omits gender identity, leaving thin formal recourse, and thin data means present police handling is uncertain. Structurally (legal since 1933, no enforcement of hostility, organised public pushback), the case extrapolates toward the low end of Reduced Risk, materially above the High-Risk band and below documented-protection jurisdictions.
